To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the loss of mossy cells after prolonged status epilepticus correlates directly with mossy fiber growth in the same animal, whereas ectopic granule cell-like neurons in the hilus are unrelated to the degree of cell loss or mossy fiber growth.
the number of hilar ectopic granules cells correlates with the severity of status epilepticus but not with the extent of mossy fiber sprout ing.
the loss of GluR 2-positive hilar neurons is associated with the development of recurrent mossy fibers and that ectopic granule-like cells increase in number in epileptic dentate gyri.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of epileptogenesis and with the role of mossy cell loss and mossy fiber sprout ing in the generation of recurrent excitation in the epileptic dentate gyrus.
the mechanisms that underlie the development of temporal lobe (hippocampal) epilepsy and the associated neuropathology.
understanding the mechanisms of epileptogenesis and with developing strategies for the prevention of epilepsy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the extent of mossy fiber sprout formation after status epilepticis is determined by the number of Glutamate receptor 2 (GluR 2) expressing hilar neurons (presumed mossy cells) that survive the initial seizure event.
the extent of recurrent sprouting of mossy fibers is correlated with the loss of mossy cells, and that the extent of mossy cell loss is correlated with the extent of moss y fiber sprouting.

mossy fiber reorganization is driven by the degeneration and/or loss of mossy cell innervation and that the number of ectopic hilar granule cells increases in response to seizure-induced cell death in the granule cell layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

status epilepticus induces the death of most GluR2-positive hilar neurons, which in turn drives mossy fiber sprout formation, and also induces the formation of ectopic granular neurons in the hilar region of epileptic rats.
mossy fiber reinnervation of the hilus is a consequence of both the loss of mossy cells and the generation of ectopic granular cells.
the loss of GluR+ hilar neurons and mossy fiber sprout formation are closely linked and that the formation of ectopic granular cells is a separate phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an inverse relationship between mossy fiber sprout formation and the number of Glur2+ mossy cells.
mossy cell death is the primary driver of mossy fiber sprouts in the epileptic dentate gyrus.
the extent of recurrent sprouting of the mossy fibers is correlated with the number of surviving GluR2(+) hilar neurons.
